## Breast Lump Assessment

**What can cause a hard lump in a woman's breast:**
The most common cause of a hard breast lump is actually a **fibroadenoma**, which is a benign (non-cancerous) firm, mobile, painless lump commonly found in young women. Other causes include breast cysts, lipomas, and fat necrosis from minor injuries. Hormonal changes during menstrual cycles can also cause temporary lumps. Breast cancer is actually a rare cause of breast lumps, accounting for only a very small percentage of all breast lumps found.

**Does every hard breast lump mean cancer:**
Absolutely **not every hard lump means cancer** - in fact, the majority of breast lumps are completely benign and harmless. A lump that is smooth, moves freely, and is painless is almost always a benign fibroadenoma that requires no treatment. Only lumps that are irregular, attached to skin, and associated with nipple discharge need serious investigation. Most women with breast lumps live completely normal healthy lives without any cancer developing.

**Other breast changes women should watch for:**
Women should regularly check for **nipple discharge**, skin dimpling, breast pain, and swollen lymph nodes under the armpit. Changes in breast size or shape should also be monitored carefully. Any **redness or warmth** of the breast skin deserves medical attention. Women above 40 should also consider regular mammogram screening examinations.

## Most Likely Cause
This woman is most likely experiencing **dysfunctional uterine bleeding (DUB)** caused by hormonal imbalance, which is the most common cause of heavy irregular bleeding in women of reproductive age with this pattern of symptoms.

## Immediate Emergency Actions
Health workers should immediately **lay her flat**, check her blood pressure and pulse, insert a large IV line, and start **normal saline or Ringer's lactate** drip to replace lost fluids and prevent shock.

The priority treatment is **IV fluid resuscitation** combined with **high-dose hormonal therapy using oral contraceptive pills** (combined estrogen-progesterone) to stop the bleeding, which works by stabilizing the uterine lining rapidly.

## First Medicine to Give
The **first injection to give** is **Syntometrine (oxytocin with ergometrine)** intramuscularly, as this causes uterine contraction and effectively controls heavy uterine bleeding regardless of the cause.
